The experiments demonstrate that GoogLeNet combined with transfer learning is the strongest configuration for image-based plant disease detection, achieving a best-case mean F1 of 0.9934 (precision, recall, and accuracy all ≈0.9935) on color images with an 80/20 train/test split, consistently outperforming AlexNet and models trained from scratch. Input representation matters significantly: color images yield the highest performance, followed by segmented images, with grayscale the weakest. Training data proportion has a monotonic effect—more training data consistently improves results—with the lowest F1 of 0.8524 observed for the least favorable combination (AlexNet trained from scratch on grayscale with only 20% training data). These results held across 30 epochs using SGD (base learning rate 0.005, step-based decay ×10, momentum 0.9), suggesting that transfer learning with modern architectures and color image inputs are the key drivers of high-accuracy plant disease classification.
